citations.claim: energy increased after first step despite no controller work
first violation step energy exceeds allowed
vy magnitude grew due to gravity integration

counterfactual.change: changed dt from 0.0213819 to 0.001 to reduce integration error; energy no longer grows and rule passes

explanation: Energy grows during free-fall with no controller and no collisions, violating energy_bound at step 4. With dt~0.021, semi-implicit Euler with substeps (~41-43 per step) still accumulates integration error: vy magnitude grows ( -38.95-> -43.98 ) while y drops (5.2->1.65), but total mechanical energy increases each step (1656.8->1830.7). Reducing dt to 0.001 removes the drift and energy stays below initial, confirming the failure is due to too-large dt causing numerical energy injection beyond the allowed 10%+5J tolerance.
vision_note: A single blue body is in clear free-fall from mid-arena toward the floor across steps 1 to 4, with no walls, waypoints, controller, or collisions visible. The visible rapid vertical drop with no interaction matches a pure gravity-driven trajectory where numerical integration could inject energy.
